The 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Washington will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the ten U.S. representatives from the state of Washington, one from each of the state's ten congressional districts. The elections will coincide with the other elections to the House of Representatives, elections to the United States Senate, and various state and local elections. Primary elections took place on August 4, 2026.[1]

Party Democratic Republican
Incumbent U.S. Representative

Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
Democratic



See also: Washington's 3rd congressional district

The 3rd district is based in Vancouver and encompasses Washington's portion of the Portland, Oregon metropolitan area. District 3 is the most competitive congressional district in the state, with a Cook PVI of R+2. The incumbent, Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, was re-elected with 51.7% of the vote in 2024.[2] In that year, she was one of only 13 Democrats to win a congressional district in a district also won by Donald Trump.[41]

Gluesenkamp Perez has received criticism from her left for her support of the SAVE Act, her vote to censure fellow Democratic Representative Al Green, and other positions.[42][43][44] In May 2025, Brent Hennrich, a stay-at-home father and candidate for this district in 2022, announced his intention to run against Perez, citing her support for the SAVE Act and the Laken Riley Act.[45]

On January 22, 2026, Representative Gluesenkamp Perez was one of seven Democrats that voted to fund the Department of Homeland Security, which includes Immigration and Customs Enforcement.[46]

See also: Washington's 4th congressional district

The 4th district encompasses much of central Washington, including Yakima and the Tri-Cities of Kennewick, Pasco, and Richland. The incumbent is Republican Dan Newhouse, who was re-elected with 52.0% of the vote against another Republican in 2024.[2]

Incumbent Congressman Dan Newhouse opted to retire instead of running for another term.[83] He initially supported Republican Yakima County Commissioner Amanda McKinney[84] before switching his support to Republican State Senator Matt Boehnke after McKinney declared her opposition to Newhouse at a TPUSA rally,[84] despite supporting Newhouse in previous bids.[85]

Republican Amanda McKinney and Democrat John Duresky advanced through the August 4 primary with 34.8% and 29.9% of the vote respectively. The 3rd and 4th place finishers, Boehnke and Republican Jerrod Sessler, have refused to endorse McKinney.[84] Traditionally conservative leaning papers such as the Yakima Herald-Republic[86] and the Tri-City Herald have endorsed McKinney's Democratic opponent. Congressman Dan Newhouse has declined to endorse either candidate.[84]
